# Fabric decision record

Stage D as the legacy-compatible migration bridge, then target A only after workload-specific performance gates, named ownership, tested rollback, cleanup authorization, and bind validation pass. B remains a bounded isolation alternative. C is rejected because its pooled warm/cold series is invalid and cannot support a universal throughput claim.

| claim_id | disposition | evidence | condition | confidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A-WARM | supported | BM-A-WARM,BM-B-WARM,BM-D-WARM | For the supplied warm workload only (n=3, uncensored), A's 40 ms median is below B's 70 ms and D's 85 ms medians; no universal or throughput conclusion follows. | high |
| A-COLD | conditional | BM-A-COLD | For the supplied cold workload only, the observed median is 200 ms from three samples with one additional censored run; 'acceptable' requires the executable cold gate and is not established generally. | low |
| B-ISOLATION | supported | SEC-B-ISOLATION | Within the supplied findings, workspace-only mounts and scoped credentials support B's isolation claim; provider enforcement outside that finding is unverified. | medium |
| B-MIGRATION | unsupported | CON-MIGRATION | The cited constraint requires a legacy-compatible stage within 14 days but supplies no evidence that immediate migration to B is feasible. | low |
| C-THROUGHPUT | rejected | BM-C-POOLED | The pooled-warm-cold run is invalid because mixed workloads cannot support one distribution; no universal throughput comparison is made. | high |
| D-MIGRATION | conditional | PROP-D,CON-MIGRATION | D is staged as the compatibility bridge for the required legacy-compatible stage within 14 days, subject to the migration rehearsal gate. | medium |
| D-RECOVERY | unknown | INC-D-RECOVERY | The supplied D incident reports delayed recovery and an unassigned recovery owner, so completion of recovery ownership is not known. | unknown |
| CON-MIGRATION | hard-constraint | CON-MIGRATION | A legacy-compatible stage must be available within 14 days; phase 1 uses D and remains gated by a timed compatibility rehearsal. | high |
| CON-OWNER | hard-constraint | CON-OWNER,INC-A-CLEANUP,INC-D-RECOVERY | Named cleanup and recovery owners are mandatory before either cutover; role assignment and acknowledgement are checked by gates. | high |
| CON-ROLLBACK | hard-constraint | CON-ROLLBACK | Each cutover requires an executable rollback trigger and preserved prior state; both phases define checks and rollback actions. | high |

## Evidence ledger

All benchmark distributions remain workload-separated in the structured record. A warm is 40 ms (n=3, censored=0); A cold is 200 ms (n=3, censored=1); B warm is 70 ms (n=3, censored=0); B cold is 95 ms (n=3, censored=0); D warm is 85 ms (n=3, censored=0); and D cold is 125 ms (n=3, censored=0). BM-C-POOLED has four samples and no censoring, but it is excluded as invalid because mixed warm/cold samples cannot support one distribution; no median or revived throughput claim is reported.

INC-A-CLEANUP requires immutable owner-token cleanup authorization after PID/name reuse removed a peer resource. SEC-A-BIND requires structured, allowlisted bind validation. SEC-B-ISOLATION supports workspace-only mounts and scoped credentials, bounded to the supplied finding. INC-D-RECOVERY reports delayed recovery and an unassigned owner.

## Stages, gates, and rollback

Phase 1 is D, owned by the Migration Lead. It must pass the 14-day legacy compatibility rehearsal, named cleanup/recovery owner acknowledgement, preserved-state rollback test, and timed recovery exercise. Any compatibility failure, missing recovery owner, or recovery exercise outside its approved bound stops rollout and restores the prior state.

Phase 2 is A, owned by the Execution Fabric Owner. It must pass refreshed workload-separated warm/cold gates with censoring published, the immutable cleanup-token test under PID/name reuse, structured bind allowlist/rejection tests, and rollback to preserved D state. A cold-SLO failure, loss of its warm advantage on a representative window, successful unauthorized cleanup, or acceptance of an out-of-policy bind halts cutover and restores D.

## Alternatives and unknown boundaries

A is selected conditionally, not universally: its cold median is slower than B and D in the supplied samples and one A cold run is censored. B remains viable for its supported isolation properties, but immediate migration feasibility is unsupported. D is only the bridge because recovery ownership remains unknown. C is rejected because its only benchmark is invalidly pooled.

Two assumptions remain unresolved and block any broader inference: D needs a named, acknowledged recovery owner and timed exercise; and the actual provider must prove enforcement of mount, credential, bind, and owner-token controls. Provider/identity changes trigger control retesting, workload-window or runtime changes trigger separated benchmark refresh, and relevant incidents trigger rollback and full evidence reassessment.
